namlish.name: Namlish
namlish.about: Namibian English as the street speaks it, laced with Afrikaans and Oshiwambo: hosh, is it?, now now, eish, lekker, sharp.

greet: Good morning! How is the morning?
Hi there, how are you keeping?
Hello Meme, how is the family?
reply: I'm fine, thank you. And you?
Fine, just a bit cold this morning.
sunny: Not a cloud in the sky again.
It's going to be a hot one today.
Beautiful day, the hills around town look golden.
Perfect weather for a braai this evening.
The sun here does not play, wear a hat.
rain: Can you smell it? Rain is coming.
Finally some rain, the farmers will be happy.
The riverbeds will be flowing after this.
Drive carefully, the roads are slippery.
First rain of the season, everyone is standing outside.
busy: Running late for work, talk later!
I must catch a taxi, see you!
Busy day at the office, I'll call you.
Meeting in town, let's chat later.

greet: Hosh hosh! Long time no see!
Morning Meme, how is the morning?
sunny: Eish, this sun is too hot!
Lekker day for a braai, hey.
Not one cloud again, is it?
Heat is too much, let's find shade.
rain: Eish, rain is coming, can you smell it?
Finally rain, the farmers will be happy!
The river is coming down, don't cross!
busy: The time is going, I must run!

sunny: Geen wolk in die lug nie.
rain: Lekker reën, ons het dit nodig.
busy: Ek is laat, sien jou later!

small_talk: Kapana at Single Quarters after work?
First rain of the season and the whole office went outside to smell it.
Cold this morning, winter in Windhoek is no joke.
Going up north to the village for the holidays.
Windhoek Lager and a braai this weekend, are we together?
The riverbed in Klein Windhoek was flowing after last night's rain.
The jacarandas are out all over town.
Taxi took the long way round Katutura dropping everyone off.
